Q: What is the minimum number of colors needed to color this graph so that no two adjacent nodes share a color?

Think step by step about what the image shows, then answer.
When you have finished reasoning, state your final answer on the last line as a single integer.

Node 2 is joined to every other node, so no other node can share its colour. That spends one colour on node 2 alone.
Setting node 2 aside, the edges that remain are 0-1, 1-3, 3-6, 6-4, 4-5 and 5-0, which form one ring: 0, 1, 3, 6, 4, 5 and back to 0. The ring has six nodes, an even number, so two colours can simply alternate around it.
That is 2 for the ring plus 1 for node 2, so the minimum is 3.
3
